newsitem.title: UK: Nigeria renews gasoline imports in petrol crisis.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria renews gasoline imports in petrol crisis.

text.p: The Nigerian government has given permission for the country's first gasoline imports in six months in an effort to end a two-week-old fuel shortage, state Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) said on Monday.
NNPC subsidiary Pipelines and Products Marketing Company (PPMC) had been given a government green light to import two cargoes of gasoline in a swap for crude oil, the Lagos-based NNPC official said.

Oil-rich Nigeria's previous gasoline imports were in September of last year but the west African OPEC producer has been forced back on to the market by a fuel shortage which brought many parts of the country to a standstill on Monday.

Nigeria last September put a stop to a crude-for-products swap which had seen it import significant volumes of gasoline and other refined products to make up for a shortfall in domestic refinery output.
Swiss trading outfit Glencore AG was the biggest supplier under the arrangement but it is not yet known who will supply the latest purchases.
Fuel shortages occur frequently in Nigeria but usually last only a few days.
Nigeria's refineries, plagued by technical difficulties, operate well below their combined 445,00 bpd of capacity.
The 125,000 bpd Warri refinery was running at 90,000 bpd on Monday because of a shortfall in crude deliveries.
And one of two crude distillation units at the Kaduna refinery has been out of action recently for repairs, an NNPC official said.
